_readme: Every entry below is marked "placeholder": true. They exist so the shop can be
built and tested, and they are deliberately generic - no real distillery is named,
because listing a brand is claiming to stock it. build.py prints a warning for
every placeholder still present, so none can reach the client by accident.

"added" is the date the bottle went on the shelf. It drives "new" on the
    card and the newest-first sort, and the arrivals feed. Format YYYY-MM-DD.
on both the card and the product page, and the image is cropped to fill it,
so shoot square or leave room around the bottle. 1200x1200 WebP is plenty.
Until an image is set the slot holds the brand mark, so the grid is already
the shape it will be once the photographs land.
"stripe_buy_button" takes a Stripe Payment Link; without one the item is still
orderable, it just goes through the order form instead of a card.

categories.name: Gin
categories.blurb: Juniper first, and then whatever the still-house could not resist.

categories.name: Whisky
categories.blurb: Malt, grain and the long argument about water.

categories.name: Agave
categories.blurb: Tequila and mezcal - smoke, earth, and a plant that waited eight years.

categories.name: Rum
categories.blurb: Cane, molasses, and the trade winds that aged it early.

categories.name: Vermouth & Aperitivo
categories.blurb: Bitter, fortified, and built for the hour before dinner.

categories.name: Liqueur
categories.blurb: Sugar with a point to make.

products.name: London Dry Gin
products.notes: Juniper-forward and unambiguous. The gin a Martini was written for.

products.name: Navy Strength Gin
products.notes: Overproof, so it survives contact with citrus and ice without going quiet.

products.name: Barrel-Rested Gin
products.notes: Six months in oak. Somewhere between a gin and a young whisky, and honest about it.

products.name: Single Malt, 10 Years
products.notes: Orchard fruit, a little malt sweetness, no smoke to argue with.

products.name: Peated Single Malt
products.notes: Coastal and medicinal. Divides a room faster than politics.

products.name: Straight Rye
products.notes: Dry, peppery, and the reason a Manhattan has a spine.

products.name: Small Batch Bourbon
products.notes: Corn-sweet and vanilla-heavy, with enough oak to stop it being a dessert.

products.name: Blanco Tequila
products.notes: Unaged, additive-free, and tasting of the plant rather than the barrel.

products.name: Espadin Mezcal
products.notes: Roasted in a stone pit, so the smoke is a method, not a flavouring.

products.name: Reposado Tequila
products.notes: Eight months in oak. Softer, and it stops fighting the glass.

products.name: Aged Rum, 8 Years
products.notes: Tropical ageing does in eight years what Scotland needs twenty for.

products.name: Overproof White Rum
products.notes: Funky, high-ester and unreasonable. Built for tiki and for float.

products.name: Rhum Agricole Blanc
products.notes: Pressed cane juice, never molasses. Grassy and faintly saline.

products.name: Sweet Vermouth
products.notes: Keep it in the fridge. Yes, really - it is wine, and it dies in a cupboard.

products.name: Dry Vermouth
products.notes: Alpine and bone-dry. The half of a Martini nobody credits.

products.name: Bitter Aperitivo
products.notes: Rhubarb and gentian, coloured somewhere between sunset and a warning.

products.name: Alpine Amaro
products.notes: Root, mint and bitterness. Drink it after everything else has failed.

products.name: Orange Curacao
products.notes: Bitter orange in brandy. The unglamorous third of a Sidecar.

products.name: Maraschino Liqueur
products.notes: Marasca cherry with the stones in. Nothing like the syrup of the same name.

products.name: Creme de Cassis
products.notes: Blackcurrant, thick and dark. One bar spoon changes a whole drink.
